# Open statements of the single proof

<!-- Generated by scripts/one_proof/render_open.py from open-statements.json (the Lean build), kinds.tsv,
claims.tsv, reviews.tsv, credits.tsv and issues.json. Do not edit by hand: edit those, or regenerate the JSON
after a fold. -->

`ZInQ.OneProof.frozenTarget` (`ZInQKernel/OneProof/Main.lean`) is a Lean theorem, checked by the kernel with no
`sorry` and only the standard axioms, that proves the frozen target `ZInQ.FrozenTarget`, the theorem that Z is
Diophantine in Q (the 11/5 manuscript, Theorem 1.1), from the hypotheses below. Everything else is proved.
Each hypothesis is a Lean `Prop`; proving one in Lean, or reducing it to statements printed in the literature,
removes it. See
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how to contribute and check a proof.

**34 hypotheses of the H part** (in the bundles `OpenAddedLeaves26`, `OpenResearchLeaves42`, `OpenTextbookLeaves17`), plus 5 hypotheses of the Tian–Yuan–Zhang and Gross–Zagier parts listed at the end.

* **Strict count: 11 published / 23 glue** (the strictest flagged reading; 12/22 without the one strictest-reading flag).
* LEAF means a published, refereed theorem stated over genuine definitions in its printed form, or a direct
  instance of it (a special case that needs no argument). GLUE is everything else: a consequence of one theorem,
  a composite of several, project glue, or a leaf whose published form is still pending a reading (`kinds.tsv`,
  column `flag`).
* By kind: consequence 10, published 24.

## Kernel-wide readings

Readings that apply to every statement built on a shared kernel definition.

* **B_dR.** The kernel's B_dR is Mathlib's `BDeRham O_Cp p`, in four textual copies, each `rfl` to it:
  `ZInQ.Contrib.G9.PkgI4.BdR` (I4Layer.lean), `BdrKer.BdR` (KerTheta.lean), `HDec.PkgI4.BdR`
  (OneProof/H/LPrefix.lean) and the KerTheta copy in OneProof/H/TailC.lean. Lean proves (KerTheta) that
  B_dR^+ = `BDeRhamPlus` is a xi-adically complete DVR with maximal ideal (xi), xi = p - [p-flat], and that
  `BDeRham` is its fraction field and is isomorphic to B_dR^+[1/xi], with the functorial G_Qp-action. The
  construction of B_dR^+ (W(PreTilt O_Cp)[1/p] completed at ker theta) is the print's (Fontaine, Asterisque 223
  Exp. II; Berger 2002 section 1.2): a definition-level reading. A print defining B_dR as Frac(B_dR^+) or
  B_dR^+[1/xi] is matched by proved lemmas (`isFractionRing_BDeRham`, `bdREquivAway`). A print defining
  B_dR = B_dR^+[1/t], t = log[eps] (Berger 2002 section 1.2), is matched only through t != 0 in B_dR^+, which
  Lean does not prove (t is not constructed in B_dR^+): a step, so a statement read through that definition is
  GLUE. No statement's rating depends on it today (deRhamH1AbVarT, the only row whose statement reaches B_dR, is
  GLUE for another reason). To close it: construct t in B_dR^+ and prove t != 0 from [eps] - 1 != 0 in W(R),
  injectivity of W(R)[1/p] -> B_dR^+ (xi-adic separatedness of A_inf) and log(1 + x) = x times a unit for x in
  the maximal ideal; then B_dR^+[1/t] = B_dR^+[1/xi] by `eq_xi_pow_mul_unit`. Fontaine's uniformizer theorem is
  not needed.

## How to help

* **Prove a statement in Lean**: pick a row whose status is open or "project interest, free to claim", claim
  it on [issue #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14) with a line `Claiming <field> at <commit>`
  (the field name as in the first column), and follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).
* **Check a statement against its printed source** (no Lean needed): pick a packet below and follow
  [STATEMENT-CHECKS.md](STATEMENT-CHECKS.md). [pages-wanted.md](pages-wanted.md) lists the printed pages a
  reader can check.
* Tiers come from a model triage that no person has reviewed yet; treat them as a rough guide.
* The project logs its folds and landings on [issue #3](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/3).

## Held

A hypothesis is held only by a public claim line, on the claims issue or in a draft pull request that links it
(the project's own holds may point at a pushed branch). A claim with no public activity for 14 days gets one
ping, and is released if there is no reply within 7 days of the ping.

## Packets

A packet is a set of statements decided by reading one block of the literature. Claim a packet with a line
`Claiming reading <packet>` on its own issue if it has one, otherwise on the statement-checks issue, and until that issue is opened on [issue #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14); see [STATEMENT-CHECKS.md](STATEMENT-CHECKS.md).

### Packet R1

Reduction block: SGA 7 I Exp. IX, BLR 1.2 Prop. 4, Serre-Tate 1968. Claim it on [Deicyde #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14).

* [`raynaudSemistableSHOr`](#raynaudsemistableshor) (LEAF): SGA 7 I Exp. IX Prop. 4.7 (Raynaud's criterion) over a strictly henselian DVR: m >= 3 invertible and A[m] rational imply semistable reduction, read over k(s) or over kbar (number UNVERIFIED); dict-models
* [`neronOggShafarevichSep`](#neronoggshafarevichsep) (LEAF; unread): Serre-Tate 1968 Thm 1 over IsSepClosure K Ks (as printed); the Kbar form proved in Lean from MulEtaleAbelianScheme (dict-galois)

### Packet R2

Unread locators: SGA 3, EGA IV, Faltings 1983 Lemma 5, GIT, BLR 1.4, 7.2, 7.3. Claim it on [Deicyde #14](https://github.com/Deicyde/diophantine-z-q/issues/14).

* [`neronSchemeExtensionDedekind`](#neronschemeextensiondedekind) (LEAF; unverified-locator): Bosch-Lutkebohmert-Raynaud, Neron models (1990), 1.4 Thm 3 with 1.2 Def 1: an abelian variety over the fraction field of a Dedekind domain D has a Neron model over Spec D (existence half; smooth, separated, quasi-compact, extension property for smooth D-schemes); numbers UNVERIFIED; group-law-dvr, goodmodel-iso. Replaces mumfordGroupLawConn (GIT 6.14 over a DVR follows: GoodModelIso.mumfordGroupLawDVR_of_dedekind) and the textbook field neronSchemeExtensionExists (its case D = O_L)

> **LEAF SHIMURA-5.4-PRINTED (the main theorem of complex multiplication, Shimura 1971 Thm 5.4, in its
> printed form).** Let `K = ℚ(√−m) ⊂ ℂ` (through `κ`, `√−m ↦ i√m`), `e : Kˢ → ℚ̄` normalized
> (`ιC ∘ e = κ` on `K`), `σ ∈ Aut(ℂ)` and `s ∈ 𝔸_K^×` with `σ = [s, K]` on `K^ab` (`ArtinCond`; it forces `σ` to fix
> `κ(K)`). Let `𝔞` be a lattice in `K` (`κ(𝔞)` is the lattice of a period pair), `E` an elliptic curve over `ℂ`
> given by a short Weierstrass model `y² = x³ + a₄x + a₆` (`E(ℂ) = E.toAffine.Point`) and `ξ : ℂ/𝔞 → E(ℂ)` an
> analytic isomorphism (`IsAnalyticUnif`, on `ℂ` with kernel `κ(𝔞)`). Then there is an analytic isomorphism
> `ξ' : ℂ/s⁻¹𝔞 → E^σ(ℂ)` (`E^σ = E.map σ`) with `ξ(u)^σ = ξ'(s⁻¹u)` for all `u ∈ K/𝔞`; here `v ∈ K` represents
> `s⁻¹u ∈ K/s⁻¹𝔞` when `s_f v − u ∈ 𝔞̂` (`s⁻¹𝔞 = sInvLat m s 𝔞 = K ∩ s_f⁻¹𝔞̂`), and `P ↦ P^σ` is `conjPt σ`.
> 
> Source: G. Shimura, *Introduction to the arithmetic theory of automorphic functions* (1971), Thm. 5.4;
> S. Lang, *Elliptic functions*, Ch. 10, Thm. 3 (numbers UNVERIFIED, from memory; not read here). Differences
> from the print, each making this statement weaker or equal: the uniqueness of `ξ'` is dropped; `E` ranges over
> short Weierstrass models only (every elliptic curve over `ℂ` has one); `𝔞` comes with a period pair. The
> notion `IsAnalyticUnif` (a group homomorphism onto `E(ℂ)` with kernel `κ(𝔞)`, holomorphic in the affine
> coordinates away from `κ(𝔞)`) is checked in Lean: by `exists_lattice_eq` and `isAnalyticUnif_iff` the maps
> satisfying it are exactly `z ↦ (℘_{L₀}(αz), ℘'_{L₀}(αz)/2)` with `E = E_{L₀}` and `L₀ = α·κ(𝔞)`, i.e. the
> analytic group isomorphisms `ℂ/𝔞 → E(ℂ)`. If the print's "analytic isomorphism" is read without the group
> law, the printed `ξ'` still satisfies `ξ'(0) = ξ(0)^σ = O` (take `u = 0`), and a biholomorphism of complex tori
> fixing `0` is a group isomorphism, so the conclusion here follows in either reading.


> **Bump–Friedberg–Hoffstein 1990, opening theorem, clause (ii), at weight `k = 2`: the
> classical newform on `Γ₀(N)`, `χ_D(n) = (D / n)` the Kronecker symbol.**
> 
> Printed statement (the statement-check read of D. Bump, S. Friedberg, J. Hoffstein, Invent. Math.
> 102 (1990), opening theorem, pp. 543–544; paraphrase): let `f` be a newform of even weight `k` and
> trivial character on `Γ₀(N)`, `ε` the sign of the functional equation of `L(s, f)`, and `S` a
> finite set of primes containing the primes dividing `N`. Then there is a fundamental
> discriminant `D` of a quadratic field with `ε D > 0`, every `p ∈ S` split in `ℚ(√D)`, and
> `L(k/2, f, χ_D) ≠ 0`, where `χ_D(n) = (D / n)` and `L(s, f, χ_D) = ∑ aₙ χ_D(n) n^{−s}` (centre
> `s = k/2`). No CM exclusion, no level condition.
> 
> Here, the direct instance at `k = 2` (centre `s = 1`):
> * `F : CuspForm ((Gamma0 N).map (mapGL ℝ)) 2` with `IsGamma0Newform F` (a cusp form of weight 2
> on `Γ₀(N)` that is an eigenform of the Hecke operators `T_n`, `(n, N) = 1`, lies in the new
> subspace of `S_2(Γ₀(N))`, the Petersson complement of the `V_d S_2(Γ₀(M))`, `dM ∣ N`,
> `M ≠ N`, and has `a₁ = 1`); trivial character is built into `Γ₀(N)`;
> * `IsFESignGamma0 F ε`: `ε` is the sign of the functional equation of the completed `L(s, F)` at
> level `N`;
> * `S : Finset ℕ` of primes containing every prime dividing `N`;
> * `Int.IsFundamentalDiscr D` (Mathlib) with `D ≠ 1`; `0 < ε * D`; `SplitsInQuadratic D S` (two
> distinct primes of `𝓞 K` above each `p ∈ S`, `K` a quadratic number field containing `√D`);
> * `KroneckerCentralValueNeZeroGamma0 F D`: `L(1, F, χ_D) ≠ 0` with `χ_D(n) = (D / n)`
> (`kroneckerSym`, the Kronecker symbol).
> 
> Source: D. Bump, S. Friedberg, J. Hoffstein, *Nonvanishing theorems for L-functions of modular
> forms and their derivatives*, Invent. Math. 102 (1990), 543–618, opening theorem (pp. 543–544),
> clause (ii).
